settings.definition_quote:
Let  $
u_1 \ldots 
u_K$ denote $K$ distributions with bounded support in $[0,1]$ with $\mu_i$ (resp. $a_i$) their mean (resp. their essential infimum). Let us further assume that $
u_i$ is lower bounded by some constant $A$ in the neighborhood of $a_i$ for $i=1 \ldots K$, and that the arm with best mean value $\mu^*$ also is the arm with best min value $a^*$.

algorithms.name: MIN (select arm with maximal empirical minimum; limit of MaRaB with alpha->0, C=0)

symbols.A_dens: constant A with P(X <= a_i + eps) >= A*eps for all arms
symbols.Delta_a_min: min over suboptimal arms of a* - a_i (essential-infimum gap)

conditions: each nu_i satisfies P(X <= a_i + eps) >= A*eps for all eps > 0
the arm with best mean is also the arm with best essential infimum

source.label: prop43
source.quote: Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the cumulative regret is upper bounded as follows: \tcr \leq \frac{K-1}{A} \frac{ \Delta_{\mu,\max} }{\Delta_{a,\min}} \log\left(\frac{t K}{\delta}\right)+  (K-1) \Delta_{\mu, \max} with $\Delta_{a,\min} = \underset{i}{\min} \, \Delta_{a,i}$ and $\Delta_{\mu,\max} = \underset{i}{\max} \, \Delta_{\mu,i}$.

results.notes: Regret R_t = sum_i n_{i,t} Delta_{mu,i} (random pull counts). Paper's t is the time index (T). MIN does not use delta, so bound holds for any delta. Proof assumes a unique optimal arm; with k optimal arms K-1 is replaced by K-k.

bound.regime: T >= (K-1)/A_dens * Delta_a_min/Delta_mu_max (as stated; the proof uses the inverse ratio)
